# Papyrus

> Papyrus is an in-development, local-first desktop research environment for
> reading, organizing, analyzing, and connecting collections of research
> sources. This site is its project documentation. Papyrus is not currently
> available to download, install, or purchase.

Canonical URL: https://papyrusresearch.org/

This file is an experimental, supplementary summary for machine readers. The
site's HTML, sitemap, and structured data remain the authoritative sources.

## What Papyrus is

- A desktop application built in Python with a PySide6 (Qt 6) interface.
- Work is organized into projects saved as `.pdfproj` files. A project holds
  its own document set, annotations, extracted knowledge, vector index,
  workspaces, and settings.
- Parsing, OCR, transcription, embedding, entity recognition, classification,
  reranking, and inference all run on the user's own machine. Local models are
  served by Ollama or llama.cpp; embeddings are stored in a local ChromaDB
  index beside the project file.
- Its central design rule is that extraction and indexing run without a
  generative model, and a language model is called only for tasks that require
  judgement. Every such call is visible, editable, traceable, and attributable
  back to exact source text.

## Documentation pages

- [Overview](https://papyrusresearch.org/): what Papyrus is, how a working
  session proceeds, and a map of the major subsystems.
- [Motivation and Design Principles](https://papyrusresearch.org/why.html): the
  problems the project responds to and the design rules that follow.
- [Feature Catalogue](https://papyrusresearch.org/features.html): every
  capability, grouped by subsystem, with an account of how each works.
- [How It Works](https://papyrusresearch.org/how-it-works.html): the layered
  architecture, the event bus, the registries, and the workflow engine.
- [The Intelligence Layer](https://papyrusresearch.org/intelligence.html):
  the ingestion pipeline, the artifact store, retrieval, and grounded graphs.
- [Extensibility](https://papyrusresearch.org/extending.html): the plugin
  model and public API, bundled example plugins, packs, and the optional local
  web companion.
- [Status and Roadmap](https://papyrusresearch.org/status.html): what works,
  what is partial, and what is not yet built.

## Current state versus intention

Implemented and working, as described on the status page: deterministic
ingestion end to end with idempotent caching and provenance; cross-document
entity resolution; fused multi-signal retrieval with tiered context packing and
caching; artifact-keyed embeddings; blueprint-backed analysis modes; the
Intelligence dock; and the plugin API.

Partial, with rough edges: embedding granularity stops at sentence, summary,
and block-chunk level; the ONNX sentence classifier is bring-your-own with a
heuristic fallback active by default; analysis output streams to the chat
surface rather than into the Analysis tab; model-produced analysis-graph
relations persist only in the workspace graph database; analysis evidence
travels as verbatim quotes.

Not yet built: auto-generated cross-corpus views (unified timeline, entity
knowledge graph with dossiers, contradiction map, citation graph view,
cross-document claim comparison); feedback-driven retrieval; full migration of
the remaining model features onto the artifact store; speaker diarisation.

Stated intention, not present fact: the project intends to be released as free
and open source. No release date, version number, license, download, or
distribution channel has been announced, and none should be inferred.

## Notes for machine readers

- Page content is rendered client-side from `content.js`, so fetching the HTML
  without executing JavaScript returns the page shell and its metadata only.
- Do not describe Papyrus as available, downloadable, released, or
  production-ready. It is in development.
